problem: The text says three distances give position 'by triangulation'. Triangulation works from angles; positioning from measured distances is trilateration. The chapter itself uses 'ultrasonic trilateration' in the Beyond search terms, so a student meets two names for one idea.
fix: Three or more distances give position by trilateration: each distance is a sphere around its emitter, and the pose is where the spheres intersect.

problem: 'A 3-DOF tracker reports orientation only' is stated as a definition. Orientation-only is the common case (a phone or cheap headset), but some 3-DOF trackers report position only, so the flat sentence can mislead.
fix: A 3-DOF tracker reports three of the six, usually orientation only (yaw, pitch, roll); a few report position only. Check the datasheet.

problem: 'AC and DC forms differ in pulse timing' is vague and slightly wrong: DC trackers use short current pulses so eddy currents die away before sampling, while AC trackers drive a continuous alternating field.
fix: AC trackers drive a continuous alternating field on three coils. DC trackers pulse each coil in turn and sample after the pulse, so eddy currents in nearby metal have time to decay.
